retrieved_evidence.source_fragment: This KEP proposes to define standard structure for Kubernetes log messages, add methods to klog to enforce this structure, add ability to configure Kubernetes components to produce logs in JSON format and initiate migration to structured logging.

This KEP proposes introducing a standardized log message structure. To enforce a new log message structure we are proposing adding new methods to the klog library: `InfoS`, `ErrorS` which will provide a structured interface for building log messages and creating new helper methods which will provide consistent identification of Kubernetes objects in logs.

With the new methods we would like also to migrate to klog v2 and introduce a new JSON logging output format to Kubernetes components that would be an alternative to the current text format and which will make querying and processing Kubernetes logs even simpler.

Taking into account the size of Kubernetes repository we will not tackle the problem of full migration to new klog methods but instead focus on improving the querability of most common logs. We will be targeting reaching a high percentage of logs in a new format generated by real cluster.

* Make most common logs more queryable by standardizing log message and references to Kubernetes objects (Pods, Nodes etc.)
* Enforce log structure by introduction of new klog methods that could be used to generate structured logs.
* Propose reasonable scope of migration:
  * Executable within SIG-instrumentation resources
  * Minimize review burden on other SIGs
  * Leave logging in acceptable state if effort fails
* Simplify ingestion of logs into third party logging solutions by adding an option to output logs in the JSON format

To allow selection of the logging output format we would like to introduce a new logging configuration shared by all kubernetes components.

`LoggingConfig` structure should be implemented as part of `k8s.io/component-base` options and include a common set of flags for logger initialization.

`--logging-format` flag should allow you to pick between logging output formats. Setting this flag will select a particular logger implementation.

Proposed flag `--logging-format` values:
* `text` for text-based logging format (default)
* `json` for new JSON format

Additionally we propose to expose to allow for customization of logging by providing custom implementation.
Custom logger format can be introduced by implementing [https://github.com/go-logr/logr](https://github.com/go-logr/logr) interface.
Registering custom implementation within `LoggingConfig` will allow to pick it by via `--logging-format` flag.
Klog interface was selected as it is already supported by klog.v2 with `SetLogger` method.

As migration to new message structure will be done manually we will be focusing on logs that have the greatest impact for log querying and processing. We will be focusing on log messages Proposed plan of measurements:

* Using log data from single run of kubernetes [gce-master-scale-performance](https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-scalability-gce#gce-master-scale-performance) tests
* Based on logs generated on master node
* Aggregate from components:
  * kube-controller-manager
  * kube-scheduler
  * kube-apiserver
  * kubelet
* Only for log lines generated by klog (e.g. prefix `I0129 03:26:19.857798       1 garbagecollector.go:517]`)
* Identified by code line that generated log (e.g. `garbagecollector.go:517`)

We assume that exact details of taking measurements can be improved, but overall methodology is solid. With those criteria we concluded that covering 99.9% of logs on master node are generated by 22 log messages. Exact list of those logs is provided in the detail design section.

test_plans.content:
## Test Plan

Aside ot standard unit tests we propose to add detailed test suite ensuring no unexpected changes in out of both logging formats implementation to ensure their future stability.

value.coverage_assessment: The existing test plan (k8s_1602) mentions a detailed test suite for both logging formats, but no concrete test cases are provided. This leaves the structured logging changes largely untested at the source level, with significant risk in areas such as format correctness, performance, and configuration compatibility.
potential_gaps: No test cases for the new klog InfoS/ErrorS methods to verify structured key-value pair formatting and error handling.
No test cases for KObj/KRef helper functions to ensure consistent Kubernetes object reference representation in logs.
No test cases for the JSON logging output format, including field names, types, and escaping.
No test cases for the --logging-format flag to validate selection between text and JSON formats and invalid values.
No test cases for the migration of high-volume log messages (e.g., HTTP access logs) to ensure no data loss or format regression.
No test cases for the LoggingConfig structure in k8s.io/component-base to validate default values and serialization.
No performance or load tests to assess log volume increase and performance impact.
No compatibility tests for existing log parsers or consumers with the new structured format.
No migration tests to ensure existing configuration options remain compatible with the new logging configuration.
recommended_missing_cases: Unit tests for InfoS/ErrorS verifying key-value pair formatting, including edge cases like nil values, empty keys, and special characters.
Unit tests for KObj/KRef covering different object types (Pod, Node, etc.) and nil/empty inputs.
Integration tests for JSON logging output validating JSON schema, field names, and proper escaping of log messages.
Tests for --logging-format flag: valid values (text/json), invalid values, and default behavior.
Tests for HTTP access log migration to ensure all fields are preserved and format is consistent.
Tests for LoggingConfig structure: default values, YAML/JSON serialization, and backward compatibility with existing flags.
Performance benchmarks comparing text vs JSON logging to detect overhead and log volume increase.
Compatibility tests with common log parsing tools (e.g., jq, fluentd) to ensure JSON output is parseable.
Migration tests for existing deployments to verify no breakage when upgrading to structured logging.
value.uncertainty: The existing test plan is high-level and lacks specific test cases, so the actual coverage is unknown. The untrusted data provided no concrete test cases, making it difficult to assess current coverage accurately.

## Feature Summary

This KEP proposes standardizing Kubernetes log message structure by introducing new klog methods (InfoS, ErrorS) that enforce key-value pairs, adding helper functions for consistent Kubernetes object references, migrating to klog v2, and adding a JSON logging output format. It also outlines a migration strategy focusing on the most common logs to minimize impact.

## Change Points

- Introduction of new klog methods InfoS and ErrorS that enforce a structured log message format with key-value pairs, changing the logging API and output format.
- Addition of helper functions KObj and KRef for consistent Kubernetes object references in logs, changing how objects are represented in log messages.
- Introduction of a new JSON logging output format via a --logging-format flag, allowing selection between text and JSON formats.
- Migration of specific high-volume log messages to the new structured format, including changes to HTTP access logs and other identified messages.
- Introduction of a LoggingConfig structure in k8s.io/component-base to standardize logging configuration across components.
